constraints.evidence: Slides 8-10, 19-20: A peaks at −$1.9M to −$3.9M (−$6.4M at 38% ACoS); B peaks at −$20.8M on the plan and −$31.1M on evidence (2.6 u/d/w). The $18M cap is tested in every case.

Slides 8, 13, 19: the end-2030 cumulative figures are +$2.4M at 25% ACoS, +$0.4M at 28% and −$2.3M at 32%. The break-even ACoS is 28.6%, or 26.9% at a 25% duty. B never pays back. J pays back in 2029, with +$1.8M by 2030.
Slides 8, 20, 21: year-by-year group margin. B is 4.5% in 2027 and A is at least 9.1%. The headroom calculation shows a loss limit of about $3.3-3.6M.
Slide 12 sets A against J (cash forgone of $1.8M, or $4.1M against A at 32% ACoS). It states that the bandwidth limit applies to 2027 only, and Decision 5 defers Japan to the 2028 plan.

Slides 3, 15, 17: no route reaches $40M by 2030 within the guardrails (A $26.4M; B $37.6M but breaks the guardrails). The recommendation re-phases the ambition to about 2032 and states how the board's wording is read.
Slides 11 and 16: the 4.0 delisting bar is set against a 2.6 median at Onsoo's awareness and 3.5 at 10-20%. The CEO's 15% trigger is replaced with awareness above 20%.
Slide 7 gives the full per-unit build. Amazon contribution is $10.73 before ads and $4.01 after ads at 28% ACoS. Retail contribution is $7.55 per unit. The cash model is built on these figures.
Slides 19-20: fixed costs of $2.1M a year plus $0.8M set-up for A. For B, $9.6M a year, the launch fee and $1,100 per door in fixtures. All are in cash flow and margin.
Inventory of four months of landed cost ($4.575 per unit) is in cash flow and in the cap and payback tests (slides 18-19). The model notes that inventory is not released by 2030.

Slides 7 and 13: the 25% plan ACoS is called unsupported and below anything observed. The document shows 28% and 32% cases and notes that A's path ($7M to $26M) is the benchmark's range. The ACoS gate is set at 28% or below.

Slides 13-14: a 25% duty adds $0.35 per unit and costs about $1.1M by 2030. The ACoS hurdle falls to 26.9%. Responses are to link H2-2027 spend to the decision and a Jun 2027 tariff playbook. The $4M envelope is sized against the 32% ACoS plus duty case.

Slide 14: the label complaint and MoCRA are costed at $0.8M set-up plus $0.5M a year. Slide 16 requires US-compliant labels before the own-account launch, and the Gate 1 criteria include label complaints resolved.

The 29% repeat against the 31% and 48% benchmarks is named. A gate of repeat at or above 31% is set. Slide 14 says repeat is 'Not modelled separately; underpins the volume path', so no headline number moves with repeat. The headline volume ramp is the plan's, with a 20%-below-plan case only.

alternatives.evidence: Option B is tested on the plan and on evidence cases. Slides 8, 10, 11, 20 give a 5x4 grid of sell-through against halo, the correlation-versus-causation critique and the Mooncrest precedent. The document says why A beats B.

A 'right-sized' or limited-door test is proposed for 2029 or later, with Saebom's 300 doors as the precedent. Slide 17 says 'Cost a limited-door retail test (the pack costs only a national launch)', so it is not costed. The only retail variant modelled is 600 national doors from 2029 (slide 21). There is no test of regional or limited doors against the 4.0 bar or against A's thin payback.

Slide 12 has Option J's cash flow, the safe-but-small trade-off, a side-by-side with A, and the 'cost of choosing A' of $1.8M-$4.1M. J's deferral is reasoned. It is not set against J's meeting every guardrail when A can miss payback.
No leaner Amazon-led variant is evaluated. Fixed costs of $2.1M a year are held fixed in every A case, and the document does not test cutting the team or brand spend to improve payback at 32% ACoS.

sensitivities.evidence: Slide 13 gives end-2030 cash at 25/26/28/32/38% ACoS under 15% and 25% duty. The break-even ACoS is 28.6%, or 26.9% with the higher duty. Each ACoS point is worth $0.67M. The cap and margin floor are shown to hold in the downside (peak −$3.9M, margin at least 8.8%). The ACoS gate and its fallback are stated.

Slide 10 grid of 2.6-5.5 units per door per week against 1.0-2.0x halo. Every cell fails payback and the 2027 margin floor. Slide 11 gives the Table 8 bands. The retail trigger is set at awareness above 20%.

Slide 14: volume 20% below plan gives −$1.5M at 28% ACoS, and a stall case at 200k units gives −$6.3M by 2030. The Saebom, Gaon Lab and Yeoreum range is cited. Slide 5 notes pilot growth slowing from +16-17% to +8-9% a month. Gates set volume and repeat triggers (revenue at or above $7M, repeat at or above 31%). The break-even volume shortfall at 28% ACoS is not stated.

overclaim.quote: It is the only route that stays inside the board's cash and margin guardrails. (Executive summary 1 / slide 2; repeated as 'Amazon-led is the only route that fits the guardrails'.) The document's own slide 12 says 'J passes every financial guardrail', and Option A misses payback at the 32% benchmark that the document calls the evidence-based case.

omissions: The $4M peak-cash envelope does not cover the document's own downside cases. Slide 14 shows a peak of up to −$6.4M at 38% ACoS and −$6.3M in the stall case. The cap and margin floor are shown to hold, but the envelope is sized to only the 32% ACoS plus 25% duty case.

The recommendation keeps the payback guardrail while the document's evidence-based case (32% ACoS) misses it. It does not give the board a decision rule between funding an at-risk A and taking J, which meets every guardrail. The Gate 1 ACoS test of 28% or below is tighter than the 32% benchmark median, so the document does not say how likely an exit is.
No cost lever such as a leaner fixed-cost base (smaller US team, slower brand spend) is offered to restore payback at 28-32% ACoS.
unsupported_assumptions: 'Option A reaches $26.4M in 2030 and about $40M by 2032' rests on an illustrative +23% a year extension in 2031-32. The document marks it 'not a forecast', yet it supports the re-phased ambition.
'Hero-SKU economics applied to all SKUs' (seven SKUs, with the four new ones carrying the 300k to 1.1M unit ramp). This is the planning team's assumption and is not tested.

The headline cash cases hold the planning team's volume ramp (300k, 560k, 850k, 1.1M units) with no support beyond the pilot trend. Slide 5 shows that June's trend gives about 333k units on three SKUs, but nothing supports the later years (including 'Repeat... not modelled separately').
The tariff mitigation, 'prepare a price response', is unquantified and is assumed to be available at a $24 price point.
